questions.prompt: What happens to Wren after she says the growing spell?
choices: She is taller than the Hollow Oak.
Her spell book is one inch tall.
questions.evidenceText: She was not taller. She was one inch tall.

questions.prompt: Why does the first spell make Wren tiny instead of tall?
choices: She had left out the final page.
She had borrowed Luna's spell book.

questions.prompt: What lesson is Wren taking into her next spell?
choices: Reading each spell carefully can prevent the same mistake.
A stronger spell is needed before reading begins.
Reading the same spell twice makes it work.
questions.answer: Reading each spell carefully can prevent the same mistake.
questions.rationale: Wren discovers that she had read the first spell backwards, then begins the next spell very carefully and forwards; this shows reading each spell carefully can prevent the same mistake.
questions.evidenceText: She began to read very, very carefully. Forwards.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: She climbed up onto it and looked at the spell. She had read it backwards.
